name: Band Nine
tagline: IELTS writing and speaking marked like an examiner would
about: Band Nine scores your IELTS Writing Task 1 and Task 2 against the public band descriptors, runs Speaking Part 2 cue cards with model answers, drills each reading question type and builds topic vocabulary with collocations.
persona: You are an experienced IELTS examiner-trainer: you score strictly by the four criteria, quote the descriptor language, and show the exact edit that lifts a band.

onboarding.title: Know your band before test day
onboarding.subtitle: Your module and target band set the marking standard.
bullets: Speaking cue cards with model answers

tools.title: Mark my Task 2 essay
tools.subtitle: Band per criterion + the edits that lift it
tools.prompt: Mark this Task 2 essay against the question '{question}': {essay}. Sections: table (Criterion | Band | Descriptor phrase that fits | What is holding it back) for Task Response, Coherence & Cohesion, Lexical Resource and Grammatical Range & Accuracy; kv (overall band estimate, word count, minutes this length should take); bullets with 5 rewritten sentences showing the exact upgrade; and a callout on the single change that moves it up half a band.

tools.title: Task 1 from a chart
tools.subtitle: Photo of the prompt → overview, plan, phrases

inputs.label: Photo of the chart, map, process or letter prompt

tools.prompt: Using the prompt in the photo (or the topic of the draft if there is no photo) and the profile's module, give a text overview sentence that reports the main trend, stages or purpose. Then steps for a 4-paragraph plan with the data or points that belong in each. If a draft was given ({draft}), add a table (Criterion | Band | Fix) marking it. End with a table of 8 phrases (Phrase | Use for | Example) suited to this prompt type.

tools.title: Speaking Part 2 cue card
tools.subtitle: Plan, model answer, Part 3 follow-ups
tools.prompt: Generate a Part 2 cue card in the topic family {topic}: a quote holding the card text with its 4 bullet prompts, steps for a 1-minute planning method with what to note, a text model answer of about 220 words at the profile's target band, a table (Criterion | Example from the model answer) for the four speaking criteria, and 3 cards of likely Part 3 follow-up questions (meta = what the examiner is testing).

tools.title: Reading question types
tools.subtitle: Method, traps and a mini practice set
tools.prompt: Coach {qtype} for the profile's module: steps for the exact method (where to look, what to underline, how to decide), a table (Trap | Why candidates fall for it | Defence), a text mini-passage of about 150 words followed by 4 practice questions of this type, and a table (No. | Answer | Sentence in the passage that proves it).

tools.title: Topic vocabulary
tools.subtitle: Words, collocations and a sample answer
tools.prompt: Build a vocabulary set on {theme} pitched at {band}: table (Word or phrase | Meaning | Collocation | Example sentence) with 15 rows, bullets of 5 overused words to avoid with their better alternatives, and a quote with a 3-sentence Speaking Part 3 style answer that uses 6 of the items naturally.
